content: I think that the theorem add_le_add_right is phrased opposite to the convention of to all the other theorems with the same name, such as Nat.add_le_add_right or Rat.add_le_add_right. Is this an error or is there a reason for this?

This topic comes up every now and then, see for example #mathlib4 > left and right. I think in this case the Nat and Rat lemmas are arguably wrong, they violate the convention that the direction should refer to the "more variable" argument, which is codified in the standard library naming conventions.
(the issue is that the incorrectly-named lemmas are in core so there has to be enthusiasm from the core team to change them, and the core team has more important things to do)
Would a PR renaming the lemma in Core be welcome in this case?

I am interested in seeing this fixed in core, but whenever I type "left" into Loogle I despair. I can agree that docs#Nat.add_le_add_left should be renamed, but what about docs#Nat.lt_of_add_left_lt ? To be consistent, we should rename that too, but I think if you consider that last lemma in isolation the name seems fine and calling it docs#Nat.lt_of_add_right_lt would feel wrong.

I have been sufficiently confused by all this that now both names feel wrong to me. This is not just left and right, but for many sufficiently complicated statements with two or more operations. Whenever I need one of these lemmas I have to check its signature to make sure it's the one I want, and I often have to use Loogle to find them in the first place. If there is any pattern I'm not seeing it.
